business.what_it_does: Lets businesses collect text and video testimonials, on autopilot or imported from other platforms, then turns them into widgets, images, Walls of Love, Reels and AI-generated case studies to share on websites, emails, ads and social posts.
business.category: Testimonial collection and social proof software
business.business_model: Subscription — free forever tier plus paid monthly or yearly plans, with per-project and per-seat add-on pricing on the Pro plan.

facts.statement: Senja is a tool that makes it easy to collect testimonials and share them anywhere, including on your website, in emails, on social media and much more.

provenance.quote: Senja is a tool that makes it easy to collect testimonials and share them anywhere, including on your website, in emails, on social media and much more.

facts.statement: The Free plan lets users collect 15 video and text testimonials, described as more generous than any competitor's free tier.

provenance.quote: Collect 15 video and text testimonials — Free. More than anywhere else

facts.statement: The Starter plan costs $29/month and includes unlimited testimonials, 3 forms, 1 project and 2 seats.

provenance.quote: Starter $29/month — Unlimited testimonials, 3 Forms, 1 Project, 2 Seats

facts.statement: The Pro plan costs $59/month and includes unlimited testimonials, unlimited forms, 5 projects and 5 seats, with extra projects and seats billed separately.

provenance.quote: Pro $59/month — Unlimited testimonials, Unlimited Forms, 5 Projects ($10/month per extra), 5 Seats ($5/month per extra)

facts.statement: Video testimonial downloads are SD quality on the Free plan and HD on Starter and Pro.

provenance.quote: Video downloads are SD on Free and HD on Starter and Pro.

facts.statement: Senja states it is used by 20,000 creators, SaaS companies and freelancers.

provenance.quote: 20,000 of the best creators, SaaS companies and freelancers collect and share testimonials with Senja.

facts.statement: The number of platforms Senja can import testimonials from is stated inconsistently across the site: 30+ on the homepage/widgets pages, 35 sources on the pricing FAQ, and 18 social media sites and review platforms specifically on the Free plan.

provenance.quote: Import testimonials from over 30 platforms / Senja allows you to import your existing screen grabs, video testimonials and text testimonials from 35 sources / Import your social proof from 18 social media sites and review platforms

facts.statement: Senja offers a developer API and an MCP integration for building custom testimonial workflows, including connecting Senja to Claude.

provenance.quote: Senja for developers — Build custom testimonial workflows using Senja's developer APIs. / How do I connect Senja to Claude with MCP?

facts.statement: Senja can generate a first-draft case study from an existing testimonial, pulling out metrics and a pull quote automatically.

provenance.quote: Senja writes the first draft for you. It pulls the metrics from the story, lifts the strongest line as a pull quote, and writes a summary and narrative that sound like your customer, not a press release.

facts.statement: Senja is a small, fully remote team led by founder/CEO Oliver Meakings, based in London.

provenance.quote: Olly is Senja's CEO and marketing cofounder. He's a London-based expert digital marketer with 20 years' experience in conversion rate optimisation. ... We're a small team working remotely around the world.

facts.statement: Senja is positioned primarily as a B2B marketing tool for businesses (SaaS, creators, ecommerce, freelancers) that need social proof for their own sales and marketing, rather than a consumer-facing product.

voice.tone: Direct and a little irreverent — it names the reader's pain bluntly, then makes a confident, almost cheeky claim about the fix. Not corporate, not soft.
voice.rhythm: Short declarative sentences, often one per line or paragraph for punch, alternating with a slightly longer sentence that explains the mechanism. Headlines read like hooks; the line right under them delivers the payoff in plain words.
voice.person: Addresses the reader directly as 'you'; the product itself is usually the actor ('Senja builds', 'Senja writes', 'Senja can help') rather than a human 'I' or corporate 'we'.

objections.objection: A wall of quotes is decoration. Show me it moved money before I put it on the critical path of my sales page.
objections.answer: Nothing in the supplied evidence answers this. Every revenue claim is either the vendor's own unmeasured assertion (E29's 'increase your conversion rates', E132's 'twice as many testimonials', E93's 'twice as many' from Spin the Wheel, E11's '3x more video testimonials' — none with methodology or baseline) or a single founder's unquantified impression (E129: Jay Clouse says he has seen tangible impact on revenue and conversion, with no numbers, period or measurement). The '+200% conversions' figure on the case study page is explicitly an illustrative example, not a customer result (E6). The only honest moves available: widget analytics report views and clicks on widgets and Walls of Love (E90), which is activity rather than revenue, and the free tier lets the reader run the test on their own page at zero cost and judge for themselves (E77, E26). Do not promise a conversion lift; offer the cheap experiment.

objections.objection: My testimonials are already scattered across a spreadsheet, G2, old DMs and screenshots. Moving them is precisely the work I have been avoiding for a year.
objections.answer: Import is the answer and it is available before paying: testimonials can be imported from CSV or from other platforms on the free tier (E24, E136, E110 names X, Facebook, Google, Capterra, Airbnb, Zillow and TrustPilot), screengrabs included (E82). If the reader would rather not touch it, there is a free concierge migration that moves everything over for them (E111). One caveat the copy must not trip over: the number of importable sources is stated three different ways across the site — 18, over 30, and 35 (E82, E127, E110) — so name the named platforms or say 'CSV and dozens of platforms', never pick one of the contested counts.

provenance.quote: Senja was a game changer for us. We we're playing with Google Sheets to handle our testimonials but it was a real mess. Switching to Senja was the right thing to do. We now have a complete platform to collect, store and display testimonials!

objections.objection: $29 a month, forever, to display quotes I already own and could paste into my own HTML.
objections.answer: Nobody has to pay to find out. The free plan is $0 forever (E77), takes 15 video and text testimonials with no credit card (E26, E79), and includes the parts that actually do the selling: unlimited widgets with over 20 templates added without code (E87), unlimited Walls of Love (E88), unlimited views (E18), case study generation (E84), Reels (E89), analysis (E83) and exports (E86). Paying only becomes necessary when they pass 15 testimonials, want Senja's branding off (E95), a custom domain (E96), HD video exports (E97) or autosync (E94). The honest frame is 'the free tier is the product; the paid plan is for when it works'.

objections.objection: The free plan is a hook. I'll collect a dozen testimonials, get attached, hit the cap and be hostage.
objections.answer: This is substantially true and should be said plainly rather than danced around: once the account hits 15, new testimonials are hidden until upgrade, though forms and widgets keep working (E112). What blunts it is that the exit is documented and cheap. Testimonials are the customer's and every plan includes exports (E116), including SD video on Free (E86). On cancellation or downgrade the account drops to Free at the end of the billing period with a 10-day grace period on paid features; testimonials stay, forms and widgets keep working, links and embeds do not break — branding returns and anything over 15 is hidden (E113). A whole project, including testimonials, forms and settings, can be transferred to another account with links and embeds intact (E125). Advise downloading HD video before downgrading, since Free exports in SD (E114).

objections.objection: Collecting testimonials isn't a software problem. The hard part is asking customers, and I'm not comfortable chasing people.
objections.answer: Partially answerable. The mechanics can be taken off them: a simple or multistep collection form in 60 seconds (E80), invites individually or in bulk with follow-ups (E81), invites triggered 24/7 (E137), automation via Zapier, API and webhooks (E138, E100), and rewards attached to the ask (E135, E93 — note the 'twice as many' figure is unmeasured). One customer reports it took under 5 minutes to start collecting and less to get them onto her website (E139). What the evidence does not solve is the reader's discomfort or the judgement of who to ask and when; the vendor's own case-study page leans on 'no interview calls or awkward follow-ups' as a benefit, which concedes the awkwardness is real. Importing proof that already exists publicly (E24) is the route that requires asking nobody.

objections.objection: An AI-generated case study will read like a press release, and the customer whose name is on it will veto it — or worse, won't be asked.
objections.answer: Partly answerable, with a gap worth naming. The draft is built from the user's own real testimonials rather than invented (E48, E46), it lifts the strongest line as a pull quote and pulls metrics out of the story (E5, E7, E6), and every word is editable before anything is shared (E49, E47) with the template built in (E51). The vendor's own claim is that it sounds like the customer, not a press release (E5) — that is their assertion, not a verified output. Nothing in the evidence describes a customer-approval or sign-off step, and the product page still shows placeholder screenshots for the editor, so there is no inspectable example output to point a sceptic at. Treat the draft as a first draft the reader edits and clears themselves.

objections.objection: We already pay for something — a testimonial tool, or Wistia and YouTube for the video. Switching is lateral movement, not progress.
objections.answer: Weakly answerable, and only with claims the reader should be told are the vendor's own. The competitive statements are all vendor comparisons: Trustmary 'integrates with a lot of platforms, but not half as many as Senja' (E17), 'the most generous free tier of any social proof tool' (E78), and 'ditch Wistia, YouTube and Vimeo' (E154) — none independently verified, and E17 gives no numbers for either side. What is checkable on Senja's own side: 23 named widget templates (E151) and four Wall of Love themes (E152), unlimited embeds and Walls of Love (E19), unlimited forms and tags (E20), unlimited tagging and filtering on every plan (E21), filtering by job title, platform or transcript (E22), unlimited ad-free video hosting built in (E150), rich snippets for star ratings in search (E36, E148), and imports available on the free tier (E24). The argument to make is 'run it alongside for free and compare', not 'they are worse'.

objections.objection: This is priced for teams. I'm one person with one website — projects and seats are an agency's problem, and I'd be paying for a structure I don't use.
objections.answer: Starter at $29/month is sized for exactly one brand: 1 project, 2 seats, 3 forms, unlimited testimonials (E91, E92). Projects and seats are only metered on Pro, at $10/month per extra project and $5/month per extra seat (E105, E106), and team access is a Pro feature (E107). A single site with under 15 testimonials needs no plan at all (E77, E79). Either plan cancels anytime (E91, E102).

objections.objection: If it doesn't work out I want my money back, and 'case-by-case' is what companies say when the answer is no.
objections.answer: There is no money-back guarantee and the copy must not imply one. What exists: refunds handled case-by-case, with billing errors, unused accounts and missed renewal notices named as fair game, a reply within 1-2 business days, approved refunds reaching the original payment method in 5-10 business days, and testimonials staying intact either way (E123). Both paid plans cancel anytime (E91, E102); downgrading keeps embeds and links working with a 10-day grace period (E113); invoices are self-serve on any paid plan (E122); switching monthly to annual is prorated by Stripe with amounts shown on the invoice (E121), and yearly billing gets 2 months free (E118). The real risk-reducer here is the free tier, not the refund policy.
